thread_title: S. purpurea ssp. purpurea District of Muskoka, ON
breadcrumb: S. purpurea ssp. purpurea District of Muskoka, ON

posts.body_html:
Purple pitcher plants from the lake district of Muskoka can get really gigantic. The original mother plants came from Art Junier, who had pitchers that were a foot long and cold hold almost a half pint of liquid! I could never get them that big, but they are certainly the most vigorous purp. purp in the collection.

posts.body_html:
Welcome to the forums, Idontlikeforums, and nice username

That's exciting to hear that the plants are maintaining strong colors under your conditions-this is definitely a very special strain of S. purpurea ssp. purpurea. In general, a lot of my purp. purps don't have much color to them since the pitchers are new, but as they age, they become darker. The yellow contrast in the hood is environmentally induced-I think it depends on your conditions.
